requirements.text: Make her close her jacket fully

outcomes.description: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
outcomes.target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.
outcomes.reference: The woman's jacket in the input image.

nodes.question: Can the woman's jacket be identified correspondingly in the source and edited images so that its front closure can be investigated?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the same woman's red jacket can be identified in both images and its approximate front region localized, even when the closure edges themselves are obscured. Fail if visible evidence establishes that the corresponding jacket is absent or that the proposed correspondence identifies a different garment. Unknown if garment identity or correspondence cannot be established. This check establishes inspection context only, not closing progress or full closure.
nodes.binding: Locate the woman wearing the red jacket in the doorway in both images. Establish correspondence using garment color, sleeves, collar, wearer, and scene context. Describe the front region relative to her torso and changed orientation, distinguishing localized but obscured closure edges from uncertain garment identity. Do not require a measurable closure change to establish correspondence.

nodes.question: Does direct inspection of the edited jacket establish that its front closure is fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible evidence establishes that the front panels meet along the entire intended closure with no remaining opening. Fail if at least one actual remaining opening along that closure is visibly established. Unknown if folds, draped fabric, pose, resolution, or occlusion prevent establishing either full closure or an actual opening. Failure to see the closure is not evidence of an opening.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited image directly for the same woman's red jacket. Use s1 only for garment identity and comparison context, not as proof of the endpoint. Identify the intended front edges and any observable closure line or genuine gap. Distinguish an opening between those edges from a loose panel, overlap, fold, or obscured surface.

nodes.question: Does comparison of the corresponding jacket fronts establish actual closing progress, after investigating whether the edited projecting panel is a closure edge, fold, or overlap?
nodes.criteria: Pass if identifiable corresponding front edges or closure segments show that the jacket has been brought together more than in the source. Fail if sufficiently inspectable corresponding closure geometry establishes that it is unchanged or more open, with no evidenced closing progress. Unknown if either closure is insufficiently visible, the panel's attachment or opposing edge cannot be identified, or change cannot be established. A pose change, projecting panel, altered silhouette, or lack of a discernible gap alone establishes neither progress nor lack of progress. This comparison does not independently establish full closure.
nodes.binding: Use s1 for garment correspondence and localization and s2 for independently observed endpoint geometry. Inspect the source's front opening and the edited jacket's intended closure, tracing the projecting red panel toward its attachment and looking for the opposing front edge and any exposed intervening region. Determine whether the panel represents a separated closure edge, a fold, an overlap, or an obscuring surface before using it in a progress comparison. Independently compare identifiable closure segments; do not repeat s2's endpoint conclusion as evidence of change. If only the endpoint is established but the source comparison is unresolved, keep progress unknown.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s2, and s3_panel_attachment. s1 establishes correspondence only and earns neither progress nor completion credit. s2 pass positively establishes full closure; return complete even when comparative progress in s3_panel_attachment is unknown or fails, since attainment of the requested endpoint does not require an independently measurable change. s2 fail positively establishes a remaining opening: return partial if s3_panel_attachment passes, absent if it fails, and unknown if it is unknown. If s2 is unknown, return unknown because the requested endpoint remains unresolved; a comparative-progress pass alone does not establish completion. If supplied evidence explicitly contains incompatible positive endpoint observations, return unknown rather than selecting a preferred observation. s3_panel_attachment now measures comparative closing progress, not the polarity of a panel-as-gap diagnostic. Unrelated changes count as no requested progress, and missing evidence must not be converted into failure or completion.
nodes.binding: Target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.. Reference: The woman's jacket in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

No unrelated constraints or mandatory techniques are added."}
